Slo-Mo engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Slo-Mo rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app high-fps capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Slo-Mo mode — Apple Camera feature that records a short moment at high frame rates — commonly 120 fps or 240 fps on supported iPhones — and plays it back in slow motion. Labeled 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, or 慢动作视频 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • High-frame-rate capture & frame buffering — capture logic that records many frames per second over a brief window, then time-stretches playback. Your listing may mention 120 fps, 240 fps, or high-fps slow motion; building capture pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Slow-playback assembly & export — post-capture processing that replays high-fps footage at normal or fractional speed for dramatic slow motion. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; slow-mo sample video production is outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVFoundation & capture sessions — camera session code configured for high frame rates with thermal and storage management. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Slo-Mo value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Slo-Mo support in the binary.

A working Slo-Mo story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Slo-Mo vs Time-Lapse vs Cinematic Mode vs Action Mode vs Live Photos vs Panorama vs Burst — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge ten Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Slo-Mo — high-frame-rate slow playback of a short captured moment — not sped-up long recording, not cinematic video blur, not portrait background blur, not motion stills, not wide stitches, not rapid still bursts, and not low-light modes:

  • Slo-Mo & high-fps slow playback (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Slo-Mo", "Slow Motion", "Slow-Mo", "High-fps slow motion", "120 fps", "240 fps", "Water splash", "Sports slow-mo", "Hair flip", "Pet jump", 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, 慢镜头, 慢动作视频. A short moment recorded at high frame rate, then played back slowly — time stretches down.
  • Time-Lapse listing copy (different) — long-duration recording compressed into a short sped-up video: Time-Lapse, Time Lapse, 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, 延时视频. Speeds long recording up — not slows a short moment down. Covered on our Time-Lapse guide.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not high-fps slow-motion marketing. Covered on our Cinematic Mode guide.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖. Video stabilization — not Slo-Mo frame-rate playback. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Live Photos listing copy (different) — still photos with a few seconds of motion before and after the shutter: Live Photos, 实况照片, 动态照片. Motion stills at normal speed — not 120/240 fps slow-mo video. Covered on our Live Photos guide.
  • Panorama listing copy (different) — wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while panning the phone: Panorama, 全景, 全景模式. Ultra-wide still stitches — not slow-motion video playback. Covered on our Panorama guide.
  • Burst listing vocabulary (different) — rapid still capture in quick succession: Burst, Burst Mode, 连拍, 连拍模式. Many still frames at once — not high-fps slow-motion video. Mention only as contrast — not the hero of this page.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light still photography — not water-splash or sports Slo-Mo demos unless your English listing shows Night Mode slo-mo specifically. Covered on our Night Mode guide.
  • Portrait Mode listing copy (different) — shallow depth-of-field still photography with soft background blur: Portrait Mode, 人像模式, 景深虚化. Subject-background separation on stills — not Slo-Mo video. Covered on our Portrait Mode guide.
  • Macro listing copy (different) — extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance: Macro, 微距, 微距近拍. Close-up detail shots — not slow-motion action video. Covered on our Macro guide.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Photo color grading — not high-fps slow playback. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.

Slo-Mo stretches a short moment into slow playback. Time-Lapse compresses hours into seconds. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. Live Photos adds motion around a still. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Burst fires rapid stills. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on stills. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Slo-Mo-specific listing copy — what translates differently

High-fps slow-playback listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Slo-Mo feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Slo-Mo phrasing

US pages use "Slo-Mo", "Slow Motion", "Slow-Mo", "High-fps slow motion", "120 fps", "240 fps", or "Capture in slow motion." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 慢动作 for the general slow-motion label, 慢动作拍摄 for capture-mode marketing, 慢镜头 for cinematic slow-lens positioning, and 慢动作视频 for the slow-playback video output. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing slo-mo capabilities your app does not support.

Capture vs slow playback

Slo-Mo marketing often shows two distinct steps — high-fps recording in progress (frame rate badge, recording timer) and finished slow playback (water splash, sports kick, hair flip). Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 慢动作拍摄 for the mode toggle, 正在录制 for recording in progress, 慢动作视频 for finished slow playback — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Use-case-specific demos

Water splash, sports action, hair flip, and pet jump each signal different buyer intent. zh-Hans overlays should name the scenario the frame shows: 水花慢动作 for water splash, 运动慢动作 for sports slow-mo, 发丝慢镜头 for hair flip, 宠物跳跃慢动作 for pet jump — not English "Water splash" pasted through machine translation without context.

120 fps vs 240 fps

When your English listing markets both frame rates, zh-Hans overlays may use 120帧慢动作 or 240帧慢动作 where the frame shows the fps badge — distinct technical claims with different screenshot vocabulary on the same product page.

Do not conflate with Time-Lapse or Burst

Slo-Mo slows a short high-fps moment down. Time-Lapse speeds long recording up into a short clip. Burst captures many stills in rapid succession. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately — 延时拍摄 belongs on Time-Lapse frames, 连拍 belongs on Burst frames, 慢动作 belongs on Slo-Mo frames.

Do not conflate with Cinematic Mode, Panorama, or Live Photos

Slo-Mo stretches a short moment into slow playback. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Live Photos adds a few seconds of motion around a still shutter moment at normal speed. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need slow-motion search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, and 慢动作视频 each signal different intent from Time-Lapse 延时拍摄 keywords or Panorama 全景 keywords.

What good zh-Hans Slo-Mo listing copy looks like

Slo-Mo-centric listings name the high-fps slow-playback workflow in plain zh-Hans — not a word-for-word mirror of English brochure lines:

  • Subtitle — one clause on slow-motion or high-fps playback outcome; room for 慢动作 or 慢动作拍摄 within 30 characters — e.g. "慢动作拍摄，定格瞬间" or "慢动作视频，高清回放"
  • Keywords — mix 慢动作, 慢动作拍摄, 慢动作视频, 慢镜头, and category nouns (摄影, 相机, 视频); avoid English-only "Slo-Mo" stuffing — see Simplified Chinese keywords
  • Description — lead with the record-high-fps-and-play-slowly workflow; mention water splash, sports, or pet jump use cases only when your app actually supports those scenarios or equivalent slo-mo paths
  • Screenshot overlays — short lines naming what the frame shows: 慢动作, 水花慢动作, 慢动作视频 — not "Slo-Mo" pasted through machine translation
  • Voice match — same 你/您 and punctuation habits as your other zh-Hans fields
  • Honest scope — if your app supports standard Camera slo-mo only but not custom frame-rate controls, zh-Hans copy should not imply pro 240 fps capture unless your English listing already claims it accurately

zh-Hans Slo-Mo captions can differ idiomatically from en-US overlays when the on-screen feature is the same — avoid mirroring comma-heavy English marketing onto iPhone art.
